A connector product carries data between other products. This page is for the company that makes one. It also covers integrations delivered through a connector, which matter to the vendors at their ends too.

## The two kinds of connector

A connector product is one of two kinds. Its product page names the kind on a chip at the top of the page.

- **Integration platform.** The customer builds the connection from a catalog of apps. Zapier, Workato and MindCloud are integration platforms. The pairs we show from an integration platform's catalog are pairs it can reach, not integrations.
- **Sync Service.** The vendor sells, runs and supports a fixed list of finished pairs. A Sync Service is listed by the pairs it delivers, not by a catalog of apps. Each pair it delivers is an integration that the Sync Service offers and owns, as [Integrations delivered through a connector](/docs/vendors/connector-vendors#integrations-delivered-through-a-connector) describes. Its product page lists those pairs under **Integrations it delivers**. On each pair's own page, its card names the company that offers it and says the two products' vendors do not offer or endorse it. It also shows the Sync Service's own rating once it has five reviews. When two or more Sync Services deliver one pair, their cards come after the others, A to Z by the company that offers each one.

### What it syncs

A Sync Service's product page has a **What it syncs** section above the pairs it delivers. It lists the types of data that move across those pairs, A to Z, each with which way it moves and on how many of the pairs. It reads the data rows on each pair, so a row you remove from a pair you own leaves it too. It also says how many pairs list no types of data yet.

The same section can show three facts: how often it syncs, who supports it, and how setup works. AEC Integrations records these facts from a page your company publishes. The section says so, with the date we recorded them and a link to that page. You cannot edit them in the portal. To add or correct one, use **Suggest a correction** on the product page. See [Requesting changes and appeals](/docs/vendors/requesting-changes-and-appeals). A fact we have not recorded is not shown, and a section with nothing to show is not shown at all.

The AEC Integrations team sets the kind. A connector we have not classified yet shows the chip **Connector**. The kind changes only the words on the site. Both kinds are connector products, and a company that makes one is a connector vendor.

## Your seat

A vendor whose products are all connectors is not invoiced for a seat. It can have a catalog-maintenance seat instead, which covers its connector listings, the products each connector reaches, and the evidence for each. In the portal, the plan panel of a connector product we hold a catalog for says the seat maintains your connector catalog, and its plan badge reads **Free**.

A Sync Service product can hold a Managed subscription, like an application. An integration platform cannot. See [Which products can hold a subscription](/docs/vendors/plans#which-products-can-hold-a-subscription).

That seat is on the Free plan. Like any Free seat, it can edit your company details and each product's description, website, logo and categories. The other product details stay with the AEC Integrations team.

We approve a connector-vendor claim like any other, and we also contact you directly about the catalog seat. [Claiming your vendor listing](/docs/vendors/claiming-your-listing) covers the claim form itself.

## The Catalog tab

The Catalog tab is for a connector product with a published catalog, which is usually an integration platform. It shows whenever we hold a catalog for your product, whatever its kind. A Sync Service with no catalog has no Catalog tab: its pairs are on its Integrations tab. The seat's work is on the **Catalog** tab of your connector product: open **Products**, choose the connector, then **Catalog**. The overview links there too. The tab lists every listing in your published catalog and which product on AEC Integrations each one is. Once we hand the catalog to your company, each match has an **Edit** button: you can change the product, rule a product out, mark a listing as outside our scope, set how confident the match is, and add a link that shows the evidence. A match you save counts toward that product's reach on AEC Integrations. Until the handover, the tab is read-only and says we maintain the catalog. A listing with no match yet gets one from us. See [Current limits](/docs/vendors#current-limits).

## If your company owns integrations

**If your company owns integrations and sells them,** it is treated as an ordinary vendor on Free or Managed, not a catalog-maintenance seat. See [Plans](/docs/vendors/plans). It can claim and edit the integrations it offers through a connector on any plan, with any seat, including a catalog-maintenance seat. [Owning an integration](/docs/vendors/owning-an-integration) explains the rest of what an owner does.

## Integrations delivered through a connector

Where a connector product carries the data and your company holds neither product, the company recorded as the owner can claim the integration, on any plan. That includes a company that sells the connector and makes neither product. Those integrations appear on your Integrations tab under **Integrations your company offers**, as a list of cards. Each card has **Open details**, which opens the integration's own page: Overview with its details and **Edit details**, **Data that's shared**, the **Change requests** sent about it, and **Settings** with retire and restore. Once you claim one, AEC Integrations stops updating it. You can then edit its details and retire or restore it, from the card or its page, on any plan. Its type is set by AEC Integrations and cannot be edited. Retiring it also stops it counting on the connector product. No company can add links to one. A Sync Service can add a new one it delivers, as below. An integration platform cannot add one. Other companies can still request a change on one that appears on their Integrations tab.

### Pairs recorded under another company

If your product is a Sync Service, its Integrations tab also lists **Pairs recorded under another company**: integrations recorded as delivered through your Sync Service whose owner on record is another company, or nobody. They are read-only. If your company is the one that offers a pair, choose **Ask AEC Integrations to record us as the company that offers this**, say why, and send. The request always comes to us, and we decide it. If we agree, your company becomes the owner and has claimed the pair, and it moves to **Integrations your company offers**. You can send one request per pair at a time.

### A Sync Service adds an integration it delivers

If your product is a Sync Service, its Integrations tab has **Add an integration** under **Integrations (your product) delivers**. Use it for an integration your Sync Service delivers between two products on the site. Neither product needs to be yours, and either may already be owned by its company. Choose the two products by name, then fill in the details: name, description, connection name, direction, listing page, documentation, pricing, pricing page, and release stage. There is no type to choose, because your Sync Service is how it is delivered.

The integration goes live without review. Your company owns it and has claimed it from the start. The vendors of both products are told that you added it. It then appears under **Integrations your company offers** on the same tab, where you add the data it syncs. If it is already on record through your Sync Service, you are told so and nothing is added. If it is retired, restore it instead.

### The data rows on a Sync Service integration

When the connector is a Sync Service, your company built and runs the integration, so it confirms the types of data it moves. Once you have claimed the integration, its card shows its rows under **Data that's shared**, on any plan:

- **Yes** confirms a row. The public page then reads "Confirmed by (your company), which offers this integration".
- **No** removes a row from the public page. It does not mark the row as disputed, because you maintain the listing.
- Pressing the answer you already gave clears it. The row then reads "Listed by AEC Integrations" again.
- **Change** moves a row to another direction. The old direction is removed and the new one confirmed.
- **Add a row** adds a type of data and confirms it. The vendors of both products are told in Messages.

If your company also makes one of the two products, the integration is on your product's Integrations tab instead. Open it, and the same controls are under **Data that's shared** on its page.

The two products' vendors cannot answer these rows. Their Integrations tab names your company as the one that maintains them. Until you claim the integration, AEC Integrations keeps its rows and you cannot change them. On an integration platform's integrations, nobody confirms the rows.

Where your company does hold a product at one end and the connection later becomes connector-delivered, the integration keeps its own page. Its Integration links section stops offering your product's group, and your existing links no longer show on the public page. They still appear in your product's group there, and you can remove them.

### When a product's vendor objects

The vendor of either product can remove an integration your Sync Service delivers from its product. Nobody reviews that removal, and it takes effect at once. The integration leaves the public site and stops counting. You are told in **Messages**, with the vendor's name and reason, under **Removed from your integrations**. You cannot restore it, and you cannot add it again: the add form tells you so. AEC Integrations' catalog updates will not bring it back either. It returns only when that vendor withdraws the removal, or when AEC Integrations ends it in one of the cases the [Listing Accuracy Policy](/legal/listing-accuracy) names. Retiring it changes nothing about the removal.

Either vendor can also report that the integration is not offered. AEC Integrations decides, and if we confirm it we take the integration off the site within five business days. And either vendor can report one wrong data flow. Once you have claimed the integration, those reports come to you in **Messages**, under **Data flow reports you received**. **Accept** changes the flow on the public page as the report asks. **Decline** leaves it. If you decline, the vendor can ask AEC Integrations to review it. Our view is advice, and you still decide the listing. A correction request under the [Listing Accuracy Policy](/legal/listing-accuracy) still applies to a data flow. If a public source shows the flow is wrong, we may take the integration off the site.
